title: Explore the seven capability categories.
intro: Choose a category for your current task. Start with a question, plan a change, build or review an artifact, then preserve the evidence and next steps.

stages.title: Research & evidence
stages.question: What question needs evidence before the project can proceed?
stages.description: Investigate the selected question, read relevant sources and mark assumptions or missing evidence.
stages.output: A source-linked question map, brief or research protocol.
stages.reflection: New information can change the question. Come back when an assumption stops holding.

stages.title: Decisions & planning
stages.question: Which option, customer or implementation shape should the project pursue?
stages.description: Compare alternatives and constraints, define an offer or choose an implementation shape with an acceptance test.
stages.output: A decision map, offer brief, placement card or ordered plan.
stages.reflection: If the options all feel wrong, go back to the person and the question before choosing again.

stages.title: Software & automation
stages.question: What application or agent extension needs to be built?
stages.description: Work from the project’s contracts, keep responsibilities separate and check the implementation against the intended behavior.
stages.output: An implementation or build plan with interface and acceptance checks.
stages.reflection: What you discover while building may change the plan. Bring that evidence back into the next choice.

stages.title: Review & testing
stages.question: Which interface, artifact or agent behavior needs review?
stages.description: Inspect the selected work, distinguish observed failures from preferences and propose a bounded revision or experiment.
stages.output: A review, targeted change or test plan with explicit evidence and limits.
stages.reflection: A new observation may call for a small revision, another prototype or a different direction.

stages.title: Writing & media
stages.question: What should your audience read, watch or explore?
stages.description: Choose the message, audience and evidence before drafting an article, talk, case study or media brief. Review the actual words, images or output.
stages.output: A sourced draft, HTML talk, case study, selected image, film plan or repeatable product-video build.
stages.reflection: If the story is hard to tell, revisit who the work serves and the choice you made.

stages.title: Migration & deployment
stages.question: What behavior must remain when the language, host or release platform changes?
stages.description: Characterize existing behavior, map the target environment and prepare migration, adaptation or deployment checks.
stages.output: A migration or release plan with parity checks and a rollback path.
stages.reflection: A move can reveal a new constraint. Return to the choice, build or improvement that needs another look.

stages.title: Memory & handoff
stages.question: Give a teammate the decisions, files, and next steps they need to continue your project.
stages.description: Preserve selected evidence, explain the current project state and coordinate ownership, access or the next action.
stages.output: A source-linked handoff, memory record, access review or focused teammate question.
stages.reflection: The next person may be you next week. What they find can become the beginning of another question.
